compareCandidate.label: Decimal vs. fraction
compareCandidate.description: A fraction writes a part as numerator over denominator (3/10). A decimal writes the same part using place value after a point (0.3). Same value, different code.

plainLanguageExplanation: A decimal is a way of showing a fraction using place value and a decimal point. Instead of writing '3 tenths' as 3/10, a decimal writes it as 0.3 — the digit 3 sits in the tenths place right after the point. The first place after the point is tenths, the second is hundredths, the third thousandths. So 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is the same as 5/10 or 1/2. Money is the decimals you use every day: $0.75 is seventy-five hundredths of a dollar. To compare decimals, compare place by place from the left. A decimal that names the same amount as a fraction is its decimal form.

whyItMatters: Decimals are how we measure money, distances, weights, and time precisely. Together with fractions and percents, decimals let you move freely between the number formats used across science, shopping, and daily life.
didYouKnow: The word 'decimal' comes from the Latin 'decimus', meaning 'a tenth' — the whole system is built on splitting a whole into tenths, hundredths, and thousandths.
compareReason: Decimals and percents both describe 'out of a hundred' — comparing 0.25 with 25% makes the connection effortless.
